ja159:1.1: “One king” (_ekarāja_) is used of an actual king at [ja303]() and [ja542](). Indra is called the “one king” at Rig Veda 8.37.3. Here, of course, it is the sun.
ja159:1.2: _Harissa_ is Vedic _haryaśva_, “yellow horse” or more commonly “he of the yellow horses”, a name of Indra. He is named such in worship of the sun and dawn at Rig Veda 3.30.12–13 and Rig Veda 3.44.2.
ja159:1.3: Commentary glosses _taṁ taṁ_ with _tasmā taṁ_, “therefore (I worship) him”, but I take it as emphatic. Also, while _taṁ_ can be “him” or “that”, here it should agree with _tayā_ in the next line, which must be “you”.
ja159:1.4: While the supplicant is singular (“I worship”), he wishes safety for all (“let us live out”).
ja159:2.6: The peacock sets out in search of fruits and flowers in his pasture.
